selection.name: Foundation 1 and the managed closures
selection.rationale: Foundation 1 is the dependency closure of a real textured sprite game: create a native game, receive its lifecycle, expose its graphics device, clear, decode a PNG into a Texture2D, submit a SpriteBatch draw, read the keyboard, exit and destroy deterministically. The selection then grows one dependency-complete closure at a time, in the order NEXT.md records. Some of those closures are pure managed and touch no native route -- the 3D transform types, the bounding volumes, the Curve family and the packed vectors; others reach CNA, as the input surface and the graphics state objects do.

provenance.authority: hash-pinned public metadata of the Microsoft XNA Framework 4.0 Windows runtime profile
provenance.note: Public contract metadata only. No Microsoft binary is stored in this repository or distributed with it. Reproduce with tools/api-compat/import-contract.py and a snapshot of the pinned hash.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game.OnActivated(Object,EventArgs)
diagnostics.detail: The protected On<Event> methods are the base class's way of raising an event a subclass may intercept before its handlers run. CNA raises the events itself, so there is no place in this projection for a subclass to stand between CNA and the handlers; the event itself is projected and these two are not.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.GraphicsDeviceManager.PreparingDeviceSettings
diagnostics.detail: The only event in the selection that carries data. It needs PreparingDeviceSettingsEventArgs and GraphicsDeviceInformation, neither of which is in the selection, and CNA's non-ext callback for it can only observe the settings where XNA's event exists to change them. Projecting the observing form under the event's name would be a quieter kind of wrong than leaving it missing.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.Texture2D.FromStream(GraphicsDevice,Stream,Int32,Int32,Boolean)
diagnostics.detail: Needs the System.IO.Stream projection. TEXTURE-2D-FROM-PNG-BYTES and TEXTURE-2D-FROM-PNG-FILE are CNA-Lisp additions over the same CNA route, and are declared as extensions rather than claimed as this member.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.Texture2D.SetData(!!0[])

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.SpriteBatch.Begin(SpriteSortMode,BlendState,SamplerState,DepthStencilState,RasterizerState,Effect)
diagnostics.detail: Needs Effect. The parameter is nullable in XNA, so a projection could accept an :EFFECT that may only ever be NIL -- which would be a fourth Begin shape XNA does not have, distinguishable from the five-parameter overload by nothing a caller could act on. It stays missing until Effect exists.

diagnostics.subject: Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.SpriteBatch.Begin(SpriteSortMode,BlendState,SamplerState,DepthStencilState,RasterizerState,Effect,Matrix)
diagnostics.detail: Needs Effect, for the same reason. Matrix exists and is complete; the effect parameter is what is absent, and CNA's own route for this overload (cna_sprite_batch_begin_with_effect) takes an Effect handle, so there is nothing to bind it to yet.
